findings.message: uses a shell-enabled process API in Python or .NET code
findings.remediation: Avoid shell execution; pass a fixed argv array and reject untrusted input before spawning.
findings.impact: Shell-enabled Python or .NET process APIs can execute attacker-controlled commands with host privileges.
findings.attack_vector: os.system/os.popen, subprocess(..., shell=True), or ProcessStartInfo.UseShellExecute=true receives untrusted input.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: writes to system directories or boot locations
findings.remediation: Restrict file writes to user-owned directories with explicit approval.
findings.impact: System startup and installation directories are sensitive destinations for persistent modification.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a boot or system directory; this low lead does not by itself prove mutation or privilege.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
